events.title: Live Aid Exhibition
events.description: Through a series of striking displays, the exhibition brings audiences on a visual journey of the Live Aid concerts, capturing the behind-the-scenes preparations, atmosphere and iconic performances by bands and artists on both sides of the Atlantic as the day unfolded. From Status Quo, U2 and David Bowie in London, to Black Sabbath and Run DMC in Philadelphia Live Aid at the National Library of Ireland immerses visitors in the scale and spirit of this iconic event from the intimacy of the National Photographic Archive. This free exhibition opens to the public daily (10.00am – 4.00pm) Readers are advised to check with the organiser before relying on the details published here.

events.title: James Joyce Walking Tour
events.description: A fun and exciting walking tour of James Joyce's Dublin offered by the James Joyce Centre. Though Joyce lived most of his life outside of Ireland, Dublin would provide the backdrop for virtually all of his work. On a stroll around the inner city, our guide will explain the real-life inspiration behind some of Joyce’s most celebrated writing, demonstrating just how central the streetscape of the ‘Hibernian metropolis’ was to the author’s life and art. The tour visits such stops as Belvedere College, the Gresham Hotel, the James Joyce Statue, Davy Byrnes, and the National Library. This is an excellent and fun introduction to Joyce in a bustling part of the city. Every Thur, Fri & Sat at 11am. Admission to the James Joyce Centre is included.

events.title: EPIC Exhibition - Common Ground: Ireland in the EU
events.description: Ireland joined the European Economic Community (EEC) – as the EU was then known – on January 1, 1973, after a referendum endorsed by 83% of voters. It was then among the poorest and most underdeveloped countries in western Europe, with a population just over half of its current size. Ireland’s accession proved to be the most consequential economic milestone in the half century since Irish independence, but it also set in motion far-reaching social and cultural change. EU legislation has driven improvements in workers’ rights, for example, and set binding targets for climate action. Irish people have studied and built new lives across Europe, while many Europeans have since made their homes here in Ireland.

Curator: Niamh MacNally, Curator of the Prints and Drawings Study Room at the National Gallery of Ireland. events.description: Our current exhibition at the National Print Museum, Come Fly With Me: Aviation, Tourism and Irish Design, uses flight as a central thread to explore how design and print helped promote Irish modernisation and position Ireland internationally. With the arrival of a number of Dutch graphic designers to Ireland in the 1950s to work on advertising for Aer Lingus, depictions of Ireland and Irishness were forever changed, as was Ireland’s relationship to Continental Europe and the US. Their design work was recognised internationally and had a huge impact on Irish design and economic development. Free admission. events.title: Rebels and Revolutionaries | Women’s History Tour
events.description: The Rebels and Revolutionaries Women’s History Tour focuses on the ones who broke out of societal shackles to make an impact around the world. Today, we are thankfully very familiar with some of these women. The likes of Mary Robinson, Ireland’s first female president, and Countess Markievicz, an instrumental figure in the 1916 Easter Rising, are well known. But many others have been largely lost to history, despite their impressive achievements. This tour draws attention to those left out of the history books, exploring how women’s stories have been hidden for many years and how, in modern times, historians have been revisiting, rediscovering and revealing these crucial pieces of the puzzle.

events.title: Exhibition: Photographs from The Ring Road – Neil J. Smyth
events.description: At the end of February 2020, weeks before Ireland’s first Covid-19 lockdown, Neil J. Smyth set off alone in a camper van on a ten-day road trip around Iceland’s Ring Road. With no schedule but his own, he followed quiet roads, lingered at abandoned buildings and walked out across snow-covered country, stopping to photograph whatever caught his eye. The exhibition presents photographs from that journey: storm clouds over sea stacks, a snowbound truck, a fuel pump glowing in the dark, red-roofed farmhouses half-lost in snow. In celebration of the Dior Fall ‘27 Fashion Show, taking place in Trinity College on 4th December under Derry-man Jonathan Anderson’s creative direction, this tour explores fascinating stories from Irish diaspora design history, including: - Wicklow woman Genevieve Figgis, the first Irish artist commissioned for Dior. - The scandal of Olympic medallist Fanny Durack wearing a form-fitting swimsuit in 1912. - Dalkey-born Carmel Snow, who became editor-in-chief of Harper’s Bazaar. Perfect for those passionate about fashion, design and the Irish diaspora’s impact on the industry.

In this, his most ambitious show yet, Jason revisits fan favourite stunts and reveals what really happened along the way. Expect the usual, but of course expect the unusual. It’s Jason Byrne, he’s going to sum up 30 years and 30 shows in one glorious fun filled show. This could be the crowning achievement from “The Outright King Of Live Comedy”. Can Jason make sense of the nonsense. You really won’t want to miss him trying.

events.title: The Dublin Card Show
events.description: Join collectors and vendors from Ireland and around the world at the award-winning Convention Centre Dublin on Saturday 27th & Sunday 28th of February 2027! The Dublin Card Show is Ireland’s biggest trading card event and we can’t wait for you to see what’s in store for the third edition! From Pokemon to Topps Premier League and beyond, no matter what you collect you’ll find it at the Dublin Card Show. Our world class venue is conveniently reachable by bus, tram, or by walking. For those who drive there is ample on-site parking. Food and drink will be available on the day.
